name: Sigma 14mm F1.4 DG DN | Art
notes: Announced 8 June 2023, on sale from late June 2023. Weight is Sigma's figure for the L-Mount version (Sony E version: 1,160 g). No front filter thread: the bulbous front element only allows a sheet-type rear filter in the holder supplied at the mount. Minimum focus 0.30 m, maximum magnification 1:11.9 and the 11-blade rounded aperture come from review/press coverage (DPReview, ePhotozine), not from a directly read Sigma spec table. Dimensions are Sigma's L-Mount figures (101.4 x 149.9 mm; Sony E: 101.4 x 151.9 mm). Launch price left null because sources still disagree: Sigma America's page was summarised as announced at USD 1,499 but retailing at USD 1,599, and reviews quote about USD 1,600. Sigma's element count is 4 aspherical elements; one review mentions three. No optical stabilisation. In September 2025 Sigma announced that the lens is renamed 'Sigma 14mm F1.4 DG | Art', with a refreshed exterior and packaging, a changed sales method and a revised price; Sigma says the optics and image quality are unchanged. The data here is for the original DG DN version; the weight and dimensions of the renamed version were not checked.
famousFor: Sigma presents it as the world's first 14mm f/1.4 lens, designed especially for astrophotography. Reviewers praised its sharpness for star fields at f/1.4.
strengths: Very bright f/1.4 aperture for night-sky work at 14mm
Sharp even at f/1.4, with aberration correction aimed at pin-point stars
Rear holder accepts sheet filters despite the curved front element
Fast, quiet HLA autofocus
weaknesses: Large and heavy at roughly 1.2 kg
Bulbous front element: no screw-in front filters, only rear sheet filters
Noticeable vignetting wide open
bestFor: Milky Way and star-field astrophotography
Auroras and night landscapes
Dramatic ultra-wide landscapes and architecture
Low-light interiors where a tripod isn't practical

name: Sigma 35mm F1.2 DG II | Art
notes: Announced 9 September 2025 as the successor to the 35mm F1.2 DG DN | Art (2019); Sigma's newer naming drops 'DN'. Sigma says it is about 20% shorter and 30% lighter than the previous model, with the filter size reduced from 82 mm to 72 mm. Weight and dimensions are Sigma's L-Mount figures (Sony E: 81.0 x 113.4 mm). The researcher found 755 g for both mounts although the ounce figures differ slightly, so the Sony E weight is unconfirmed; the audit's searches did not recheck this lens. Sigma also mentions high-refractive-index glass but gives no count, so it is not listed in specialElements. Maximum magnification is Sigma's 1:5.3 ratio (also quoted as 0.19x by reviews). focusMechanism 'floating' reflects Sigma's description of two focus groups each driven by its own HLA motor. No optical stabilisation.
famousFor: A second-generation f/1.2 35mm that Sigma made much smaller and lighter than the original, bringing an ultra-fast aperture to a size closer to conventional f/1.4 primes while improving sharpness and autofocus.
strengths: Very sharp, contrasty centre even at f/1.2
Smooth bokeh with clean specular highlights
Much more compact and lighter than the first-generation 35mm F1.2
Fast dual-HLA autofocus in continuous mode
weaknesses: Still larger and heavier than most f/1.4 35mm primes
Premium price for a 35mm lens
No optical stabilisation
bestFor: Low-light concerts and music photography
Environmental portraits with shallow depth of field
Documentary and wedding coverage indoors
Street photography at night

name: Sigma 85mm F1.4 DG DN | Art
notes: Announced 6 August 2020. Sigma confirms 5 SLD + 1 aspherical elements, an 11-blade rounded diaphragm, a 77 mm filter, a 630 g weight and a 94.1 mm length (the Sigma text found does not say which mount these figures refer to; diameter not found, so dimensionsMm is null). From review sources (ePhotozine), not directly from Sigma: 15 elements, minimum focus 0.85 m, maximum magnification about 1:8.4 (stored as 0.12), and the GBP 999 UK launch price. Groups left null because review sources disagree: ePhotozine gives 10 groups, while a search summary of other review pages gave 15 elements in 11 groups; Sigma's own spec table could not be read. famousFor: Sigma's mirrorless-only redesign of its 85mm f/1.4 Art, far smaller and lighter than the older DSLR-era 85mm F1.4 DG HSM Art while keeping very high sharpness. It costs less than most first-party 85mm f/1.4 lenses for the same mounts.

name: Sigma 105mm F2.8 DG DN MACRO | Art
notes: Announced 30 September 2020, on sale October 2020; Sigma's first macro lens in its mirrorless Art line. Weight and dimensions are Sigma's L-Mount figures (Sony E: 710 g, 74 x 135.6 mm). Autofocus motor left null: search summaries of Sigma pages repeatedly named an HSM (Hyper Sonic Motor), which may be a mix-up with the older 105mm F2.8 EX DG OS HSM Macro and could not be confirmed. famousFor: Sigma's first macro lens for its mirrorless Art line. Reviewers noted very high sharpness at life-size magnification for a moderate price.
strengths: Very sharp at both macro and normal distances
True 1:1 magnification with internal focusing and a fixed length
Dust- and splash-resistant build with a water- and oil-repellent coating
Good value for its optical performance
weaknesses: Autofocus can hunt, especially at close range
No optical stabilisation for handheld macro work
bestFor: Life-size macro of insects and flowers
Product and jewellery photography
Tight head-and-shoulders portraits
Copying artwork, documents and film negatives

name: Sigma 70-200mm F2.8 DG DN OS | Sports
notes: Announced 16 November 2023, on sale 7 December 2023 at USD 1,499. OS2 stabilisation is rated at 7.5 stops at the wide end and 5.5 stops at the tele end (Sigma); the wide-end figure is stored. Weight is Sigma's L-Mount figure (the Sony E version is about 10 g lighter). Internal zoom, Arca-Swiss foot and several AF-stop buttons
weaknesses: Heavier than the lightest first-party mirrorless 70-200mm f/2.8 zooms

name: Sigma 300-600mm F4 DG OS | Sports
notes: Announced 24 February 2025; release was delayed and it went on sale in April 2025. Listed as '300-600mm F4 DG OS Sports (else 150-600mm DG DN)'; the 300-600mm exists, so it was researched. Note that its name has no 'DN', although it is designed for the L-Mount and Sony E mirrorless mounts. No front filter thread: it uses a drop-in holder for 40.5 mm filters, so filterMm is null. Weight and dimensions are Sigma's L-Mount figures (Sony E: 3,970 g). The Sigma figure found does not say whether the weight includes the removable Arca-Swiss-compatible tripod foot, so treat it as possibly including it. Sigma also mentions anomalous-dispersion and high-refractive-index glass without counts, so these are not listed in specialElements. Maximum magnification is 1:6 at 470 mm. OS is rated at 5.5 stops at 600 mm. The USD 5,999 launch price comes from review coverage (PetaPixel, DPReview), not from a Sigma page. Internal zoom per review sources. Construction (28 elements in 21 groups, 6 FLD, 1 SLD), 2.8-4.5 m minimum focus, 40.5 mm drop-in filter, 3,985 g and 167 x 467.9 mm were rechecked against Sigma's pages. Sigma reports that it received the EISA Ultra-Telephoto Zoom Lens 2025-2026 award and a TIPA World Award 2025.
famousFor: A zoom that keeps a constant f/4 aperture from 300mm to 600mm. Reviewers found it gives much of the performance of a 600mm f/4 prime with the option to zoom out to 300mm, at a much lower price than first-party 600mm f/4 primes.
strengths: Constant f/4 all the way to 600mm
Very sharp, even wide open
Effective 5.5-stop optical stabilisation at 600mm
Zoom flexibility that a 600mm prime cannot offer
weaknesses: Very heavy at about 4 kg, heavier than first-party 600mm f/4 primes
Large and expensive; practically needs a monopod or tripod
Only drop-in 40.5 mm filters, no front filter thread
bestFor: Bird and wildlife photography at dawn and dusk
Field sports and motorsport from the sidelines
Air shows
Safari photography from a vehicle with a bean bag

name: Sigma 500mm F5.6 DG DN OS | Sports
notes: Announced 20-21 February 2024 alongside the 15mm F1.4 DG DN Diagonal Fisheye; on sale in the US from mid-March 2024 at USD 2,999. Weight is the L-Mount figure (48.3 oz / about 1,370 g); another Sigma figure found gives 1,365 g without naming the mount, so the Sony E weight is unconfirmed. According to The-Digital-Picture, the weight includes the detachable Arca-Swiss-compatible magnesium tripod socket; a weight without it was not found. Dimensions are Sigma's headline figures (mount not stated). Sigma says the design reaches its compact size with large low-dispersion elements and no diffractive (DO/PF) elements. OS2 stabilisation is rated at 5 stops. Maximum magnification is 1:6 (stored as 0.17). Sigma's 1.4x and 2x teleconverters are supported on the L-Mount version only (review sources). The audit reconfirmed on Sigma's pages the HLA motor, 5-stop OS2, 95 mm filter and the absence of diffractive elements, but not the 20-element / 14-group construction, the FLD/SLD counts or the F32 minimum aperture; the special-element list may be incomplete. The TIPA 'Best Super Telephoto Prime Lens' 2024 award is reported by Sigma's press centre.
famousFor: An unusually compact and light 500mm prime for mirrorless cameras, at about 1.4 kg and small enough to use handheld, while staying sharp from corner to corner at f/5.6. It was named Best Super Telephoto Prime Lens in the TIPA World Awards 2024.
strengths: Very compact and light for a 500mm prime, easy to handhold
Sharp across the frame even at f/5.6
Fast, quiet HLA autofocus
5-stop OS2 stabilisation; teleconverter support on L-Mount
weaknesses: f/5.6 gathers less light than heavier 500mm f/4 primes
Fixed focal length is less flexible than 150-600/200-600mm zooms
Teleconverters work only on the L-Mount version
bestFor: Handheld bird photography on long hikes
Wildlife from hides and vehicles
Outdoor field sports and motorsport
Aviation and air-show photography
